title: Storm-damaged parks and closed Kula gym
summary: FEMA left parks facilities out of reimbursement for the 2026 storms and the state appealed. The Kula gym remains closed with only one $1.9 million bid to tarp it and no repair timeline, and the Parks Department agreed to keep the council informed.

timeline.text: Repair costs may be repaid six to nine months after full invoices go to FEMA.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A member asked the Parks Department to keep the council informed about the Kula gym, and the department agreed.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Parks said it has no timeline yet for the gym.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Parks said there is no other gym close by for Kula kids to use.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: A Kula resident asked whether the gym will be rebuilt, and when.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: The department said FEMA left parks out of its categories of work for this storm event.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Only one contractor bid to tarp the open part of the gym, at $1.9 million.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee

timeline.text: Storms damaged county parks, and the Kula gym remains closed.
timeline.body: County Council Water Authority, Social Services, and Parks Committee
